passage:
Okay, so this was last term, in our class chat. Devika sent a long message about her science project, and it had one spelling mistake. Then a row of laughing faces started. Six, seven of them. Somebody wrote "typo queen".
I'm Urmila, and I read every reply and typed nothing. My thumb hovered. I thought, if I say something they will turn on me. So I put the phone down and ate my lunch, and my rice tasted of nothing.
That evening I messaged Devika alone: "That chat was unkind. I'm sorry I stayed quiet. Your project sounds great." She wrote back, "Thank you for saying that."

qa.q: How many laughing faces did the class chat show after Devika's message?
qa.a: A row of laughing faces started, six or seven of them.

qa.q: Why did Urmila type nothing while the laughing faces piled up?
qa.a: Urmila was afraid that the others would turn on her too. The hovering thumb and the tasteless lunch show she felt uneasy and guilty about staying quiet.

qa.q: What did Urmila do that evening, and what else could a bystander try in the chat itself?
qa.a: Urmila messaged Devika privately to say the chat was unkind and to apologise for staying quiet. In the chat a bystander could also change the subject or ask a plain question about the project.

qa.q: How might Devika have felt when the laughing faces began and later when Urmila wrote privately?
qa.a: Devika probably felt embarrassed and small at first, and then a little comforted by Urmila's private message. Saying "Thank you" shows the kindness reached her.

grounding: A student watches classmates mock a member's message with laughing faces and stays silent in the chat, then offers private support.

passage:
I sit behind Nilesh in class, and I saw him on Friday during free period. Someone posted a screenshot of Ritika's message in our class chat, and laughing faces started stacking up under it. I could see Nilesh's screen over his shoulder. He read it, very still, and did not add a face.
Then Nilesh typed, "Did anyone get the maths sheet for Monday?" Two people answered. The faces stopped.
After the bell, Nilesh walked to Ritika's desk and said something quiet. Ritika nodded. I don't know what he was feeling, but he looked uncomfortable all the way home.
— Gargi

qa.q: What did Nilesh type to the class chat after reading the screenshot?
qa.a: Nilesh typed, "Did anyone get the maths sheet for Monday?"

qa.q: What might Nilesh have been feeling while sitting very still and not adding a face?
qa.a: Nilesh seems to have been uneasy and unwilling to join in. Gargi cannot know for sure, but the stillness and the uncomfortable look on the way home suggest it.

qa.q: What did Nilesh do that helped Ritika, and why did it work?
qa.a: Nilesh changed the topic to the maths sheet, so people had something else to answer and the faces stopped. Then Nilesh spoke quietly to Ritika at the desk after the bell.

qa.q: What might Ritika have felt when Nilesh came to the desk after the bell?
qa.a: Ritika may have felt relieved and less alone, since the nod suggests the quiet words were welcome. Being singled out in the chat is painful, so a private kindness matters.

grounding: A student watches classmates mock a member's message, does not join in, changes the topic and offers private support, as seen by someone sitting behind.
